prompt: Let $A$ be a set and $R\subseteq A\times A$ a binary relation on $A$. For $x,y\in A$, write $R(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in R$. Which condition defines irreflexivity?

answers.explanation: No element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted.
Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. This defines reflexivity, not irreflexivity.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. This defines symmetry, not irreflexivity.

answers.text: $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\;\forall z\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(y,z))\Rightarrow R(x,z))$.
answers.explanation: Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices. This defines transitivity, not irreflexivity.
At least one self-loop is absent; other self-loops may be present. This defines failure of reflexivity, not irreflexivity.
No ordered pair is present, including between distinct elements. This defines emptiness, not irreflexivity.
Every related pair has no reverse. Taking the two elements equal also forbids loops. This defines asymmetry, not irreflexivity.

answers.text: $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(y,x))\Rightarrow x=y)$.
answers.explanation: Mutual relatedness forces equality. Self-loops are allowed. This defines antisymmetry, not irreflexivity.
Some related pair lacks its reverse; this is an existential violation. This defines failure of symmetry, not irreflexivity.
Every related pair is diagonal; some or all loops may be missing. This defines coreflexivity, not irreflexivity.
